question: What is Monsoon Fire Pottery?
answer: Monsoon Fire is a production-first ceramics studio in the West Valley. We work out of a 2,500 sqft basement studio plus 1,000 sqft of garage and outdoor workspace, built for steady firing, quiet making, and dependable support.

question: Who is the studio for?
answer: We are most useful for production potters and serious hobbyists who need dependable firing and workspace. If you are brand-new to clay and want structured group workshops, we can point you to great Phoenix studios. If you want focused, independent time, you will feel at home here.

question: How is Potter of the Month selected?
answer: Potter of the Month features are selected from active studio clients and working potters moving through the kilns. It is a studio-curated feature rather than an open nomination.

question: How do I get the address and gate code?
answer: We share the exact address and access details through the portal once your account is verified and you have approved visit context. The legacy reservation system is being decommissioned during May 2026 and reaches end-of-life on May 31, 2026. Create a free portal account here.

question: How do I submit a firing request?
answer: Submit a firing request through the portal with your clay body, glaze notes, firing type, and any deadline you need reviewed. You will see the current scheduling estimate band there too.

question: What are the kiln firing prices?
answer:
Half shelf = about a carry-on suitcase laid flat. Tall pieces need clearance; handles waste space; stacks are more efficient. If you are unsure, send a quick photo and we will help estimate. We bill by per-shelf or whole-kiln only; we do not bill by kiln volume.

  • Full Kiln (or custom fire) — $60
  • Half-Shelf Bisque — $15
  • Half-Shelf Glaze — $25
  • Community Shelf — $0 (lowest priority, space permitting, with shelf-owner permission, and excluded from firing triggers)
  • Delivery — $25 per trip

question: Do you offer credits if there is a firing mistake?
answer: Yes. If review shows the issue was studio-side, we apply generous credits to the affected firing service. Maker-side issues like clay, construction, glaze behavior, or firing-direction problems are not automatically credited.

question: How do I estimate how many half shelves I need?
answer: If your work fits laid flat inside a carry-on, that is about one half shelf. Tall pieces need clearance; handles and irregular shapes take extra room; stacks (like plates) are more efficient. When in doubt, ask and we will help size it.

question: How often do you fire?
answer: We generally fire at least once per week and add extra loads when demand is high, but posted firing windows are estimate bands rather than guarantees. Most weeks include both bisque and mid-fire glaze firings.

question: What kiln do you use?
answer: We fire in an L&L eQ2827-3 electric oxidation kiln with a Genesis touch screen controller, rated to cone 10. A raku reduction kiln is planned for the property.

question: Do you load the kiln for me?
answer: Yes. Kilns are loaded by studio technicians so spacing, supports, and kiln furniture are handled safely and consistently.

question: What is a day pass?
answer: Day passes are $40 and include appointment-only access to studio equipment and work areas after staff confirms your visit window. Request access through the portal or support so we can confirm your visit before sharing access details.

question: What is happening to memberships?
answer: Membership is being decommissioned during May 2026 and reaches end-of-life on May 31, 2026. Studio services are moving toward direct firing, access, and support workflows instead of recurring membership.

question: How do payments work?
answer: Firing services are charged when work is accepted into service. Supplies and other online payments still run through Stripe, and in-person payments can be handled by tap-to-pay POS. If a studio-side firing mistake is confirmed, we apply generous credits after review.

question: How often are workshops offered?
answer: Workshops are occasional and announced when the studio schedule allows. Details are posted through the portal and public studio updates when a session is ready.

question: Can you pick up supplies for me?
answer: Yes. Clients can request supplies through support or the portal and pick them up during a staff-confirmed visit window, or ask for delivery.

question: Do you offer reduction firing?
answer: Not yet. A raku reduction kiln is planned for the property, and we will announce it through the portal when it is ready.
